edit.description: Catch ResetKeepRefusedError (and other throws) at both primary-checkout afterMerge-revert call sites (~1686 singleton, ~2148 fanout); surface as a handled tick/entry fact, never an uncaught crash, so the wave still reaches commitPendingUpdate for already-merged siblings.

A resetKeepTo collision during a fanout wave's per-entry afterMerge revert, after a sibling entry already merged, does not crash the tick; the sibling still ships via commitPendingUpdate. Same coverage for the singleton leg.

summary: resetKeepTo's collision refusal is uncaught at both primary-checkout revert sites, crashing the tick after sibling wave entries already merged.

per.section: Tip verify — one writer per branch, absorption at the merge

tests: a ResetKeepRefusedError during a fanout wave's per-entry afterMerge revert does not crash the tick; already-merged sibling entries in the same wave still reach commitPendingUpdate and ship
a singleton tick's afterMerge-revert collision surfaces as a handled outcome, not an uncaught process crash
acceptance: Neither primary-checkout resetKeepTo call site can propagate an uncaught throw out of the tick; a collision is reported as a fact and sibling wave entries already merged still get their pending.json rewrite.
notes: Audit finding against shared-checkout-keep-reset (6cb9948): resetKeepTo's own refusal is left uncaught by its two callers, reproducing via a new path the queue-behind-tree hazard 'Absorbing the ledger commit' closed — already-shipped siblings' pending.json rewrite never runs if the crash happens first.

edit.description: harvestFriction's base-delta probe (git.readFileAtRef, ~2923-2932) gets the same try/catch-and-log-per-item handling as its sibling readdir/mkdir/rename failure modes, instead of propagating uncaught.
A git.readFileAtRef failure while probing one candidate friction file's base-delta status is logged and does not abort teardown of the wave's remaining worktrees/branches.

summary: harvestFriction's new base-delta probe has no error handling, so one probe failure aborts the whole wave's teardown instead of isolating to that file.
tests: a readFileAtRef failure during the base-delta probe is caught, logged per item, and does not abort the wave's teardown of remaining worktrees
acceptance: harvestFriction's base-delta probe failure is isolated per file, matching every other failure mode in the function; teardown of remaining worktrees/branches in the wave proceeds regardless.
notes: Audit finding against friction-harvest-base-delta (418234d): the new probe is the only failure mode in harvestFriction without a try/catch, contradicting 'harvest failure never aborts the wave.' Accepted separately as debt: a file modified-but-present at base is silently excluded — matches spec's literal 'untracked, or absent from the base tree' wording, not a divergence.

edit.description: The startup sweep's worktree-base enumeration (~3061-3070), when this.opts.namespace is unset, must not treat every top-level entry under a shared FLUME_WORKTREES_DIR as this instance's own residue — scope removal to entries this job's own naming actually owns.
An unnamespaced instance's startup sweep, run against a shared FLUME_WORKTREES_DIR holding a live namespaced sibling job's worktree directory, leaves that sibling's directory and branches untouched.

summary: An unnamespaced instance's startup sweep can delete a sibling namespaced job's live worktree directory under a shared FLUME_WORKTREES_DIR.

per.section: Startup sweep — a dead wave's residue is removed at the next start

tests: an unnamespaced instance's startup sweep does not remove a sibling namespaced job's worktree directory or branches under a shared worktree base
acceptance: The startup sweep removes only directories/branches this job's own naming owns; a sibling namespaced job's live worktree tree survives an unnamespaced sweep of a shared base.
notes: Audit finding against startup-sweep-residue (7036f2f): when namespace is unset, sweepBase's readdir enumerates every top-level entry including a sibling namespace's subdirectory, and removeWorktree's win32 rm -rf fallback deletes it outright — contradicts 'removes only its own job's directories... by the same namespace.'
